newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends steady, cargoes to U.S. digested.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends steady, cargoes to U.S. digested.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended steady on Monday as traders counted up the cargoes heading to the U.S. from both Northwest Europe and the Mediterranean.
Traders said it appeared the arbitrage was closed on Monday for regular unleaded material after NYMEX gasoline futures edged slightly lower.
Eurograde barges were last heard unchanged at $215 fob ARA and regular unleaded was steady to a shade higher at $214/$217, traders said.
The arb lifeline to the U.S. has helped offset what some traders said was lacklustre local demand.

Med traders said 1.0 to 1.5 million tonnes, or about 8.5 to 12.7 million barrels, of unleaded gasoline were sold from there to the U.S. in the first half of January after the arbitrage swung wide open. And healthy demand was still visible.
In addition, the U.S. appetite was believed to have gobbled up supplies from NWE as well.
"I think it's well over a million tonnes from NWE," said one London trader. "If you look at the imports on the APIs, it's entirely possible."
He said the arbitrage from NWE to the States was still open for low octane material, but was doubtful for regular unleaded and impossible for grades above Eurograde.
"It's very clear the low octane is short," he said, adding there was an oversupply of the higher octane gasoline.
